record.title: The reader owns motion, contrast, scheme and text size

record.title: A large model stays interactive

record.title: A failure can be caught and understood
record.rule: Every failure the library raises carries a stable code, that code is listed in a shipped table with its cause and its remedy, and the declared type enumerates the codes instead of naming a bare string.

record.title: Changes are validated against an unchanged context
record.rule: A change requires an unchanged context receipt; a stale context, unknown field or broken reference is rejected and the source file is preserved.
when: A change is applied through the API or CLI.

record.title: What a version promises is written down
record.rule: The package states its license, records every release in a changelog, and says which contract versions a package version accepts and what a contract change costs a consumer.
when: A version is published.

record.title: One snapshot, one set of definitions
record.rule: Every statement has a single definition; all views render the one selected snapshot.
when: A model is loaded or rendered.

record.title: Imports point down one table
record.rule: Imports point down one layer table and never form a cycle, and the browser surface performs no file or network access outside its single loader.
when: A module is added or moved.

record.title: Every document is generated
record.rule: Every shipped document is generated from the snapshot and regenerating it in place is a no-op; drift fails the check instead of being repaired by hand.
when: A document is generated or checked.

record.title: Model content is inert
record.rule: Model content renders as literal text: no executable markup, no active-content links, and no request outside the declared model and asset reads.
when: Model content is rendered.

record.title: A result rests on the definitions its check named
record.choice: Record basis.definitions on a result and withdraw it only when one of those definitions moves or its bound source bytes change; a result naming no definitions falls back to the whole contract digest.
alternatives: Hold every result to the whole contract digest, so any edit anywhere withdraws every receipt.
record.because: Holding a run to the whole contract makes every receipt stale on the next unrelated edit, so a project either stops recording runs or re-runs all of them to say nothing new.
consequences: A receipt states the contract it read rather than the contract of the day, so verification compares it to the basis the result names.
A result goes with the check it reports on: when the check loses currency the run is withdrawn as DEPENDENCY_CHANGED, naming the check.
A result must carry a stored snapshot manifest, or its scope cannot be read and it is withdrawn.

record.choice: Derive how a node and a relation are drawn - tone, shape, outline and line - from one table keyed on the rendering contract's closed enums, and read that table from both the map and the generated diagram; a renderer adds only its own pixels.
alternatives: Style the map in its stylesheet and leave the generated diagram as one flat rectangle per node.

record.title: What went stale, and why
record.change: Report every record that lost its basis with the definition that moved, as a reading list the author can work through.

record.title: Withdraw only what depended on it
record.change: Compute a per-definition basis so a changed definition withdraws its dependents instead of every basis in the snapshot.

record.title: Canonical digest for the basis
record.choice: Compute basis.contract as a SHA-256 over a canonical representation of the definitions, excluding results, history and review text.
alternatives: Track freshness by timestamps or manual review flags.
record.because: A content digest detects real definition changes without trusting order or edit metadata.
consequences: Any definition change, including additions, drops the current basis.

record.title: A question is a first-class record
record.change: Surface every question-origin source as an open list in the map and the documentation, so an unanswered question is not filed as a fact.

record.title: A claim has an age and an author
record.change: Record when a claim was written and by whom, and show a claim older than its stated life as ageing rather than as current.

record.title: Compare two snapshots
record.change: Add a diff that reports added, removed and changed records between two snapshots, and what lost its basis as a result.

record.title: A rejection that teaches
record.change: Point every validation failure at the record, the field and the value it read, and state the accepted shape beside it.

record.change: Generate a table of every failure code with what it means and what to do, from the same module that raises them, and publish it in the shipped documentation.

record.change: Add a command that writes a minimal valid snapshot with a scope, a source, a requirement and a criterion, so authoring never starts from an empty file.

record.title: Terms and history in the package
record.change: Add the licence the package claims and generate the release history from the snapshot, so what changed between two versions is readable without Git.

record.title: Shipped copies say they are copies
record.change: Rename the shipped model and copy assets so a consumer cannot mistake them for their own project file, and release the change as a break.

record.title: Project data and copy stay external
record.choice: Load model data and UI copy as external resources rather than bundling them into the library.
alternatives: Embed a default model and copy in the shipped scripts.
record.because: The format stays independent of any project, repository or build, and shipped scripts do not carry project data.

record.title: What a version promises
record.change: Write down which exports, contract fields and asset paths are public, what a minor and a major change may do to them, and check the package against that list.

record.title: Grade a contract change
record.change: Compare the shipped contract with the previous one, grade the difference as additive or breaking, and refuse a snapshot from a newer major with a named failure.

record.title: Start from the shipped page
record.change: Generate the install, mount and first-failure walk-through from the model, with the exact commands and the mounting snippet a consumer copies.

record.title: A failure is a picture, not an empty frame
record.change: Show a rejected or unreachable model as a stated failure inside the mounted surface, with the code, the record and the remedy.

record.change: Run an accessibility audit and a keyboard walk-through in the browser harness and fail on a violation instead of on a screenshot review.

record.title: The reader owns the surface
record.change: Honour reduced motion, forced colours, colour scheme and text zoom, and keep the map usable when the page reflows to one column.

record.title: Say what changed
record.change: Announce a loaded model, a selection, a level change and a failure through a live region, so a change the reader did not type is not silent.

record.title: The map under a keyboard
record.change: Make the map a single tab stop with arrow traversal, enter to select, escape to leave a container, and the same reach a pointer has.

record.title: Focus that can be seen

record.title: Measure the budget, do not assert it
record.change: Add a harness that loads a generated model of the stated size and records first response, interactive and full-layout times against the stated parameters.

record.title: Layout leaves the interface thread
record.change: Run ELK in a worker, keep the last good geometry while a new one is computed, and cancel a superseded layout.

record.title: Ask for a layered graph rather than place boxes
record.choice: Compute geometry with the ELK layered algorithm - the Sugiyama pipeline - loaded on demand, and treat its output as the only source of position and size.
alternatives: Store coordinates in the snapshot and let an author place each box.
record.because: A dependency graph read top to bottom needs layer assignment and crossing reduction, both solved by a stated algorithm, and hand-placed coordinates would make arrangement a fact nobody validates.
consequences: Layout cost grows with the model, so it has to move off the interface thread to keep the response budget.
A reader cannot nudge a box; a bad reading is fixed by changing the model or the layout options.

record.change: Mount only the parts inside or near the viewport and release the rest, so a hundreds-of-parts model does not keep every node alive.

record.title: A legend that cannot drift
record.change: Render the legend for the map and the generated diagram from the appearance table, so a new enum value appears in it without anybody writing it down.

record.title: Never colour alone

records.title: Archivarius
records.purpose: One validated JSON file - a snapshot - holds a project's whole description as small linked records: its parts, the rules they must satisfy, the decisions behind them, the work left and the checks that confirm it. A React library draws that file as an architecture map that reveals more detail as it is zoomed.

records.title: Purpose of the library
records.statement: An owner understands a system's structure, the grounds for decisions, the remaining work and the effect of changes from one snapshot; an LLM reads and edits the same records.

records.title: The repository describes itself
records.statement: The snapshot in this repository describes Archivarius itself, so the map below, the tables under it and this page are the project's own records drawn by the library it documents.

records.title: Provenance and freshness model
records.statement: Observed in this repository: a record keeps the definitions it was written against apart from the records it merely mentions, and when one of those definitions moved, everything resting on it lost currency in the same run while unrelated records kept theirs. Held to the whole snapshot instead, one edit withdrew all thirteen receipts at once - a withdrawal that named nothing and taught nobody anything.

records.title: Model and contract
records.summary: Owns the v4 JSON schema, record types, graph references, revision provenance, snapshots and the validated-change contract; storage may be inline, adjacent archive segments or committed Git versions.

records.title: Core
records.summary: Parses and validates a model, projects a v4 project to an architecture, and analyzes freshness and completion.
records.boundary: Layout and rendering stay outside the core.

records.title: Graph references
records.summary: Validates typed relations between records and reports reverse links and coverage.
records.boundary: Reference semantics are fixed by the schema targets.

records.title: Canonical digest
records.summary: Computes the SHA-256 basis over a canonical representation of the definitions.
records.boundary: The canonicalization rules are internal to the digest.

records.title: Node API
records.summary: Reads model files and Git-backed history, verifies evidence, applies validated changes and generates documentation.

records.title: CLI
records.summary: Exposes init, validate, read, context, apply, reference, readme, documents, graph, diff, history, verify, reconcile, run, archive and git-history over the model file.
records.boundary: Argument parsing and file paths stay inside the CLI. git-history migrates committed history without changing commits or the index; normal file commands read it through the Node API.

records.title: Evidence verification
records.summary: Matches declared binding bytes against files and records actual check outcomes.
records.boundary: Executing checks is performed by the run command, not by loading a model.

records.title: Map rendering
records.summary: Draws an interactive architecture map with confirmation, outstanding work and attention signals on its components; full records open on request.

records.title: Architecture map
records.summary: Draws components and interactions on the full canvas with semantic zoom. Wheel, pinch and keyboard navigate framed hierarchy levels; cards and edges carry their own meanings. There are no floating camera controls, minimap, breadcrumbs or duplicate connection lists. Component details and connections open in the inspector.
records.boundary: Layout geometry stays inside the map.

records.title: Contextual inspector and records
records.summary: Keeps a short component summary beside the diagram. Readers follow tasks and evidence without losing the map, and open full records, project lists or documents on request.
records.boundary: Project data and UI copy stay external resources.

records.title: Model source
records.payload: A v4 JSON snapshot as a URL, File, Blob or parsed object.
records.meaning: Any accepted source resolves to one parsed snapshot before anything renders, and a snapshot that fails validation is never partly displayed.

records.title: Change input
records.payload: A context receipt and a change with put and remove sets.
records.meaning: The receipt fixes the definitions the change was written against, so a change computed from definitions that have since moved cannot land.

records.title: Evidence artifact
records.payload: Relative binding paths and the bytes they resolve to.
records.meaning: A declared path confirms only while its bytes still match, so an artifact that was moved or edited stops confirming on the next read.

records.title: Reference set
records.meaning: Every relation resolves to an existing record of a type its field allows, and whatever nothing points at is reported as uncovered.

records.title: Basis value
records.payload: The canonical definitions and their SHA-256 basis.
records.meaning: Equal definitions yield an equal basis whatever their order or edit history, so a differing basis means a definition really changed.

records.title: Record detail
records.payload: A selected record with its links and implementation outcome.

records.title: Stale or invalid changes are refused

records.title: Confirmation needs byte-exact evidence
records.rule: A check outcome confirms only with an available execution artifact and matching bytes for every declared input; missing or stale evidence does not confirm.
when: An implementation outcome is derived.

records.title: Stale and missing evidence cannot confirm
records.assertion: A result confirms only when its artifact exists and every declared input's bytes match; otherwise the criterion is not confirmed.

records.title: Conservative freshness

records.title: Dependents are marked for review

records.title: Canonical digest for the basis
records.choice: Compute basis.contract as a SHA-256 over a canonical representation of the definitions, excluding results, history and review text.
alternatives: Track freshness by timestamps or manual review flags.
records.because: A content digest detects real definition changes without trusting order or edit metadata.
consequences: Any definition change, including additions, drops the current basis.

records.title: One appearance table for every picture
records.choice: Derive how a node and a relation are drawn - tone, shape, outline and line - from one table keyed on the rendering contract's closed enums, and read that table from both the map and the generated diagram; a renderer adds only its own pixels.
alternatives: Style the map in its stylesheet and leave the generated diagram as one flat rectangle per node.
Ship the palette as a consumer-facing asset beside the UI copy.
records.because: A second palette drifts, so the same zone or interaction kind would read differently in the map than in the generated documentation, and a value the contract allows could reach a renderer with no display token at all.
consequences: A value added to a contract enum fails the appearance suite until it is given a token.
The table carries tones, shapes, outlines and lines; a fill, a text colour, a dash length and a radius stay with the surface that draws them, so the generated diagram leaves both to the reader theme.

records.title: A team adopts the library
records.statement: A team installs the library, mounts a map of its own system, and needs to find how to install it, how to read a failure and what it may rely on across versions.

records.title: A reader works with a keyboard and a browser of their own
records.statement: A reader arrives with a keyboard, a screen reader, a text size, a motion preference and a colour perception the library does not choose, and a link is how a finding is passed to somebody else.

records.title: A real system outgrows one screen
records.statement: A described system reaches hundreds of parts, layout runs on the same thread as the interface, and every part stays mounted whether it is visible or not.

records.title: Bytes cannot see meaning
records.statement: Observed in this repository: with every binding digest holding, reconciling the described interactions against the import graph still found three dependencies the description could not state and two hundred and fifty-three it never mentioned. A digest proves a file has not moved, not that it still does what a record claims, so agreement of description and code is read from the code and not inferred from bytes.

records.title: Detail arrives by zooming
records.rule: Zoom input moves directly between useful views of the same map: the overview, a framed container with its children, and a readable leaf when more magnification is needed. One wheel or pinch gesture enters at most one new hierarchy level; its inertia does not keep drilling. Zoom-out returns to the containing level and stops at the overview. A leaf has no further zoom states once it is readable. Container expansion follows legibility thresholds with hysteresis during the transition.
when: A reader zooms with the wheel, pinch or keyboard.
exceptions: A container with no children never expands.

records.title: A view can be handed to somebody else
records.rule: Every view a reader reaches - focus, expansion, open panel - is addressable by a link that restores it, and the same view leaves as an image without a screenshot tool.
when: A reader shares what they are looking at.

records.title: Everything reachable by pointer is reachable by key
records.rule: Every action a pointer can take a keyboard can take: one tab stop per region, traversal between parts and their relations inside the map, and focus returned to the control that opened a panel.
when: A reader navigates without a pointer.

records.title: A change the reader did not type is announced
records.rule: A change the reader did not type - zoom, expansion, focus, a panel opening or closing, a load failing - is announced to assistive technology.
when: The view changes without a keystroke that caused it directly.

records.title: The reader owns motion, contrast, scheme and text size
records.rule: The map honours the reader motion, contrast, colour-scheme and text-size settings, and no fact is carried by colour alone.
when: The map is rendered.

records.title: A failure can be caught and understood
records.rule: Every failure the library raises carries a stable code, that code is listed in a shipped table with its cause and its remedy, and the declared type enumerates the codes instead of naming a bare string.
when: The library refuses to load, validate, apply or render.

records.title: A consumer starts from the shipped documentation
records.rule: A consumer can install the package, mount a map, style it and validate a model from the shipped documentation alone, without reading the source.
when: A consumer adopts the library.

records.title: What a version promises is written down
records.rule: The package states the terms it grants, records every release in a changelog, and says which contract versions a package version accepts and what a contract change costs a consumer.
when: A version is published.

records.title: A large model stays interactive
records.rule: Layout and geometry run off the interface thread, only visible parts are mounted, and a model of the stated size reaches first paint and stays interactive within the stated budget.
when: A model larger than one screen is loaded.

records.title: Every read is bounded and cancellable
records.rule: Every read bounds what it accepts - a size limit on input, a timeout on layout, a cap on concurrent artifact reads - and every bound is reported as a coded failure rather than a hang.
when: Input is read from a file, a URL or a caller.

records.title: Authoring starts from something valid
records.rule: A new project starts from a generated skeleton, every record type has a template, a change can be rehearsed without writing, and every diagnostic names the field and the fix.
when: A project is created or edited.

records.title: A claim binds to what it rests on
records.rule: A claim binds to the parts of the code it rests on - several files, and a range within a file - so an unrelated edit does not withdraw the confirmation.
when: A record is bound to code.

records.title: Withdrawal follows dependency
records.rule: A definition change withdraws confirmation from the records that depend on it, and a review confirms a subtree without re-reading the whole project.
when: A definition changes.

records.title: Two snapshots can be compared
records.rule: Two snapshots of one project can be compared: what was added, removed, re-zoned, re-parented, re-confirmed or withdrawn, as a report and on the map.
when: A snapshot is compared with an earlier one.

records.title: A description is reconciled with the code
records.rule: A described relation is reconciled against the dependency the code actually has: a declared edge that no longer exists and an existing edge nobody declared are both reported.
when: Evidence is verified.

records.title: A claim can be aged and questioned
records.rule: Every record states when it was last changed and by whom or what, so a claim can be aged, attributed and questioned.
when: A record is written.

records.title: An outcome comes from running something
records.rule: A check declares the command that proves it, an outcome is written only by running that command, and a hand-written pass is refused.
when: A check outcome is recorded.

records.title: Model content is inert
records.rule: Model content stays inert: no executable markup, active-content links or requests beyond declared model and asset reads. Document strings may display code and emphasis, and relative links may navigate only to document records already present in the validated model; unknown and external destinations remain literal text.
when: Model content is rendered.

records.title: Imports point down one table
records.rule: Imports point down one layer table and never form a cycle, and the browser surface performs no file or network access outside its single loader.
when: A module is added or moved.

records.title: Every document is generated
records.rule: Every shipped document is generated from the snapshot and regenerating it in place is a no-op; drift fails the check instead of being repaired by hand.
when: A document is generated or checked.

records.title: English is the only language
records.rule: The library ships English copy only: no locale parameter, no translation table beyond the shipped copy, and the mounted subtree states its language.
when: Copy is read or rendered.

records.title: A snapshot can leave the library
records.rule: A snapshot leaves the library as a standalone diagram, a self-contained page and an image, each generated from the same projection the map draws.
when: A snapshot is published outside the map.

records.title: A part can be found by name
records.rule: A reader finds a part by name from the map itself and the map moves to it, and a filter hides what is out of scope rather than only dimming it.
when: A reader looks for a part.

records.title: The map answers where an effect reaches
records.rule: The map answers where the effects of a part reach: the path between two parts, the transitive dependents of one, and the cycles between them.
when: A reader asks what a change touches.

records.title: Zoom stops at meaningful views
records.assertion: One wheel gesture reveals the pointed container in place; an uninterrupted burst or continued pinch does not skip another level. Keyboard commands use the same framed destinations. A further inward gesture enters a nested container or makes a small leaf readable; repeated inward input at a readable leaf leaves the camera unchanged. Outward input returns to the containing frame in one step and cannot shrink beyond the overview. Zoom-in never reduces scale, including when a single root already fills the overview. Announced levels, expansion hysteresis, pan, explicit entry, return navigation and restored addresses remain usable.

records.title: A link restores the view
records.assertion: Opening a shared link restores the focus, the expanded containers and the open panel, and the map exports the current view as a vector and a raster image.

records.title: No action needs a pointer
records.assertion: Every control and every part is reachable and operable by keyboard, the map is one tab stop with traversal inside it, and closing a panel returns focus to its opener.

records.title: Untyped changes reach assistive technology
records.assertion: A zoom, expansion, focus, panel or failure change is published to a live region naming the new state.

records.title: Reader settings survive the map
records.assertion: With reduced motion, forced colours, a dark scheme or doubled text size the map stays usable, and every zone, kind and relation kind reads without colour.

records.title: Every code is documented and typed
records.assertion: Every code the library can throw appears in the shipped code table and in the declared code union, and no undocumented code is reachable.

records.title: A consumer mounts from the docs
records.assertion: The shipped documentation carries install, mount, stylesheet, asset-path and validation instructions that run as written.

records.title: A release states what it promises
records.assertion: The package states its terms - `UNLICENSED`, granting nothing, and no licence file in the tarball - ships a changelog entry per version and states the contract versions it accepts.

records.title: A stated size stays interactive
records.assertion: At the stated node count layout runs off the interface thread, only visible parts are mounted, and first paint and interaction stay inside the budget.

records.title: A bound is reported, not hit silently
records.assertion: An input over the size limit, a layout over the timeout and an aborted read each fail with their own code and leave no work running.

records.title: Authoring starts and fails helpfully
records.assertion: A generated skeleton validates, every record type has a template, a rehearsed change writes nothing, and every diagnostic names the field and the fix.

records.title: A binding narrows to what it claims
records.assertion: A record binds several files and a range within a file, and an edit outside every bound range leaves the confirmation standing.

records.title: Withdrawal is proportionate
records.assertion: A definition change withdraws only dependent records, and a subtree review restores currency without touching unrelated records.

records.title: A comparison names what moved
records.assertion: Comparing two snapshots reports each added, removed, re-parented, re-zoned and re-confirmed record, and the map can show the difference.

records.title: Declared and actual edges are reconciled
records.assertion: Verification reports every declared relation the code no longer has and every dependency the code has that no record declares.

records.title: A record carries its age and author
records.assertion: Every record states its last change time and author, and both survive a round trip through apply and archive.

records.title: Only a run can pass a check
records.assertion: A check without a command is refused, and an outcome written without a matching execution artifact does not confirm.

records.title: Content cannot act
records.assertion: HTML, script URLs, images and unknown or external links in model content stay text and trigger no requests. Document code and emphasis are inert elements; known relative document links navigate within the loaded model.

records.title: The import graph stays a directed layer table
records.assertion: The import graph is acyclic and points down the layer table, and no module outside the loader reads a file or the network.

records.title: Regeneration is a no-op
records.assertion: Regenerating every shipped document leaves the bytes unchanged, and a hand edit is reported as drift.

records.title: One language ships
records.assertion: The shipped copy declares English, no exported function takes a locale, and the mounted subtree states its language.

records.title: A snapshot renders outside the map
records.assertion: A standalone diagram, a self-contained page and an image are generated from the projection and open without the library.

records.title: Search moves the map
records.assertion: Searching from the map finds a part by name and moves the view to it, and a filter removes out-of-scope parts from the canvas.

records.title: Reach is answered on the map
records.assertion: The map reports the path between two parts, the transitive dependents of a part and any cycle among them.

records.title: Detail as a function of interest
records.statement: Furnas, Generalized Fisheye Views, CHI 1986 (https://doi.org/10.1145/22627.22342): a display that holds full detail near the point of interest and degrades it with distance shows a structure larger than the screen, so how much detail a part gets is a function of interest rather than a separate view the reader has to open.

records.title: One zoomable surface with representations that change
records.statement: Perlin and Fox, Pad, SIGGRAPH 1993 (https://doi.org/10.1145/166117.166125), and Bederson and Hollan, Pad++, UIST 1994 (https://doi.org/10.1145/192426.192435): on one continuous zoomable surface an object may change its representation at a size threshold - semantic zoom - which replaces a stack of separate diagrams with a single space.

records.title: Zooming alone loses the context it hides
records.statement: Cockburn, Karlson and Bederson, A Review of Overview+Detail, Zooming, and Focus+Context Interfaces, ACM Computing Surveys 2009 (https://doi.org/10.1145/1456650.1456652): pure zooming costs the reader the surrounding context and the memory of where they were, so a zoomable map owes them an overview and a way back to a named position.

records.title: The tasks a reader of a structure performs
records.statement: Shneiderman, The Eyes Have It, IEEE Symposium on Visual Languages 1996 (https://doi.org/10.1109/VL.1996.545307): overview first, zoom and filter, details on demand, then relate, history and extract - seven tasks, and a viewer that omits one of them leaves the reader without a move.

records.title: A notation is judged by its visual variables
records.statement: Moody, The Physics of Notations, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 2009 (https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.2009.67): a visual notation is judged by perceptual discriminability, dual coding and one symbol per concept, so shape, outline and tone must carry a meaning together instead of colour carrying it alone.

records.title: Geometry is read more accurately than hue
records.statement: Cleveland and McGill, Graphical Perception, Journal of the American Statistical Association 1984 (https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1984.10478080): position and length are decoded more accurately than area or colour, so anything a reader must compare belongs in geometry and colour stays a label.

records.title: Layout says things the notation never states
records.statement: Petre, Why Looking Isn't Always Seeing, Communications of the ACM 1995 (https://doi.org/10.1145/203241.203251): arrangement carries meaning the notation never states and only a practised reader sees it, so a generated picture must not let accidental placement stand in for a stated fact.

records.title: Hierarchical layout is a solved, stated algorithm
records.statement: Sugiyama, Tagawa and Toda, Methods for Visual Understanding of Hierarchical System Structures, IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics 1981 (https://doi.org/10.1109/TSMC.1981.4308636), shipped as the layered algorithm this library asks ELK for (https://eclipse.dev/elk/reference/algorithms/org-eclipse-elk-layered.html): layer assignment, crossing reduction and straightening make a dependency graph readable without anybody placing a box by hand.

records.title: Three response budgets a reader can feel
records.statement: Card, Robertson and Mackinlay, The Information Visualizer, CHI 1991 (https://doi.org/10.1145/108844.108874): 0.1 second reads as a direct response, 1 second keeps a train of thought unbroken and 10 seconds is the limit of held attention - the budgets any layout sharing the interface thread has to fit.

records.title: One architecture, several views
records.statement: Kruchten, The 4+1 View Model of Architecture, IEEE Software 1995 (https://doi.org/10.1109/52.469759): one architecture is described by several views written for different concerns, so several documents rendered from one snapshot answer more than a single diagram trying to answer everything.

records.title: A module hides a decision
records.statement: Parnas, On the Criteria to Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, Communications of the ACM 1972 (https://doi.org/10.1145/361598.361623): a module exists to hide a decision behind its interface, which makes a layer table and a one-way import rule part of the description of the design rather than a lint preference.

records.title: A rejection names the rule it broke
records.statement: Meyer, Applying 'Design by Contract', IEEE Computer 1992 (https://doi.org/10.1109/2.161279): a component states its precondition, so a caller that violates one can be told which obligation it missed instead of receiving an anonymous failure.

records.title: Accessibility is a stated conformance list
records.statement: W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), with the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/): keyboard operation, a cue that is not colour alone, contrast, reflow, a respected motion preference and an announced status change are numbered success criteria and named widget patterns, not matters of taste.

records.title: Status and errors in the reader’s language
records.statement: Nielsen, 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design (https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/): visibility of system status, user control, and error messages that state the problem in plain language and suggest a remedy.

records.title: A dated dialect and a graded change
records.statement: JSON Schema 2020-12 (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core) and Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html): the contract is declared in a dated dialect and every change to it is graded, so a consumer can tell an addition from a removal before upgrading.

records.title: A diagram is defined by its level and its audience
records.statement: Brown, the C4 model for visualising software architecture (https://c4model.com/): context, container, component and code are levels of one description with different audiences, which is what a zoom threshold has to correspond to if the map is to replace them.

records.title: No fact is carried by colour alone
records.rule: Every distinction the map or a generated diagram draws - zone, kind, interaction, selection, staleness - is carried by at least two of tone, shape, outline, line and text, and the text form alone is enough to read it.
when: A node, a relation or a state is drawn in the map or in a generated diagram.
exceptions: A purely decorative surface that states no model fact.

records.title: A second channel exists for every distinction
records.assertion: For each value of every drawn contract enum the appearance table names a non-colour channel as well as a tone, and the panel states the same value in words. Legible collapsed cards name kind and zone beside their shape and colour; confirmation marks have visible words. Relation labels include their kind when space permits and use compact typed counts for same-kind bundles. The browser needs no separate legend to decode these labels.

records.title: Ask for a layered graph rather than place boxes
records.choice: Compute geometry with the ELK layered algorithm - the Sugiyama pipeline - loaded on demand, and treat its output as the only source of position and size.
alternatives: Store coordinates in the snapshot and let an author place each box.
records.because: A dependency graph read top to bottom needs layer assignment and crossing reduction, both solved by a stated algorithm, and hand-placed coordinates would make arrangement a fact nobody validates.
consequences: Layout cost grows with the model, so it has to move off the interface thread to keep the response budget.
A reader cannot nudge a box; a bad reading is fixed by changing the model or the layout options.

records.title: Read a system nobody explained
records.actor: An owner new to the system
given: A validated snapshot of a system with more parts than fit on one screen is mounted.
steps: Read the overview and the component names on the diagram.
Search for a part by name.
Zoom into it in one gesture to reveal its children in place.
Follow one relation to a neighbour and read the closure of what a change to it reaches.
Copy the address and open it again in a new tab.
failures: A name that matches nothing states so instead of clearing the map.
An address naming an absent record is refused with a stated failure.

records.title: Read the map with a keyboard and a screen reader
records.actor: A reader using a keyboard, a screen reader and a reduced-motion setting
given: A validated snapshot is mounted in a browser with the reader’s own settings.
steps: Reach the map by tab and traverse it by arrow key.
Select a part and read the panel.
Change the level and hear what changed.
Enlarge the text until the page reflows to one column.
failures: A part reachable by pointer but not by key fails the run.

records.title: Install it and mount a first map
given: Only the published package and its generated documentation are available.
steps: Follow the shipped page to install the package.
Write a first snapshot from the starting template.
Mount the map in an application and feed it that snapshot.
Break the snapshot on purpose and read the failure.
Upgrade to the next version and read what the version promised.
failures: An input past the stated bounds is rejected by name, not by exhaustion.
A snapshot from a newer major contract is refused with the grade of the difference.

records.title: Confirm, withdraw and compare
given: A snapshot with recorded outcomes and bound parts is loaded.
steps: Run a check and store its output as evidence.
Change one definition and read what lost its basis and why.
Read the described part against the file it binds to.
Compare the snapshot with the previous release.
Export the result for a tool outside the library.
failures: An outcome with no recorded run is refused.
Moved bytes ask for a reading instead of staying confirmed.

records.title: Regenerate every document
given: A validated snapshot and the committed generated documents are present.
steps: Regenerate the landing page, the reference and every diagram.
Parse each diagram with the renderer that will draw it.
Compare the result with the committed files.
Confirm a record carrying markup is drawn as text.
failures: Any drift between the model and a committed document fails the run.

records.title: Levels a reader can name
records.change: Move wheel, pinch and keyboard commands between framed hierarchy destinations, skip redundant camera stops and stop at readable leaves or the overview. Share target selection in the zoom model and framing with explicit focus. Keep one transition per continuous gesture, announced levels and expansion hysteresis.
records.reconsideredBecause: The owner requested removal of peripheral zoom icons, the minimap, Whole system navigation and the duplicate Archivarius Documentation banner. Navigation remains through the diagram, gestures and keyboard; connection reading uses the existing inspector. This updates the design and verification contract, without asserting new execution receipts.

records.title: Navigate through the diagram
records.change: Keep hierarchy navigation on the diagram through wheel, pinch, container entry and keyboard commands. Return to the containing frame through outward zoom or Escape, and to the full view through Home or the host home method. Remove the separate minimap, its camera history button, breadcrumbs and camera toolbar; use the full drawing area with symmetric padding.
records.reconsideredBecause: The owner requested removal of peripheral zoom icons, the minimap, Whole system navigation and the duplicate Archivarius Documentation banner. Navigation remains through the diagram, gestures and keyboard; connection reading uses the existing inspector. records.title: The view lives in the address
records.change: Encode selection, zoom, level and filters in the address, restore them on load, and reject an address that names a record the snapshot does not hold.

The model integration check now exercises committed migration, retained failures, receipts, missing commits and clones without sidecars; no execution results are asserted by this review.

records.assertion: Wheel zoom in both directions produces only compact and complete fact views for each collapsed card, including at phone width and with doubled text size. A full project card reveals kind, zone, confirmation words, criterion meter and attention or task counts together; no scale shows only a subset of these facts. Expanded container headers never grow a duplicate fact summary. Cards do not preview an arbitrarily ordered task or reveal interface lists at another zoom threshold. Parent task counts include assigned descendant work once and exclude unrelated sibling tasks. A verified result changes card evidence; missing proof does not draw a failure. A container opens its parts with one explicit button as well as semantic zoom and keyboard navigation, without also opening the inspector. Following a task from the component summary keeps the map visible on desktop and Back restores the selected component. Titles and visible facts stay within card bounds. Full records, lists, documents and history remain reachable on request.
